title: Perplexity API Pricing in 2026: Models & Costs
summary: Perplexity API pricing structures rely on a combination of model-based token rates and fixed surcharges for each web-grounded query performed.
body_markdown:
## Calculate Perplexity API token and search costs


### The 2026 Sonar model price table


Choosing between lightweight extraction and deep reasoning gives you granular cost control. The following table breaks down the current rates for the Sonar model family.


Model Input Price (per 1M tokens) Output Price (per 1M tokens)


Sonar Small $0.20 $0.20


Sonar Large $1.00 $1.00


Sonar Pro $3.00 $15.00


Sonar Reasoning Pro $5.00 $15.00


*Prices and plan limits checked against[docs.perplexity.ai](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/admin/rate-limits-usage-tiers) on October 12, 2026.*


96% is the amount you reduce your input costs by when choosing Sonar Small over Sonar Reasoning Pro, allowing your high-frequency monitoring tasks to remain profitable at scale, so your operational budget stretches significantly further under heavy workloads.


### Distinguishing between online and offline model versions


The $5 surcharge for every 1,000 requests is not a universal tax on every model listed in the table, meaning users are not automatically billed for standard offline interactions.


Perplexity distinguishes between "online" versions, which actively crawl the web to provide grounded answers, and "offline" versions, which function as standard large language models.


When you call an offline model, you only pay the standard token rate for input and output. This allows you to use the same Sonar architecture for internal data processing or creative writing without triggering the search fee.


You only opt into the $5 per 1,000 requests premium when your application specifically requires the real-time retrieval capabilities of the online model variants, so costs remain low for static tasks.


### Invoking specific model behaviors


Developers control the search surcharge by modifying the model string or the search parameter in their API request.


To invoke the offline version of a model like Sonar Large, you must use the specific model name without the online suffix, ensuring the system treats the request as a standard inference task.


If your integration uses a library that defaults to search, you can explicitly disable the web-crawling feature by setting the search_type parameter to chat instead of internet.


This programmatic distinction ensures that your automated workflows only pay for grounded data when the specific logic of the step requires live information.


### Understanding the $5 per 1,000 search requests fee


Every time an API call triggers a web search, you incur a flat $5 per 1,000 requests fee, which adds a predictable $0.005 overhead to each grounded response, ensuring budget projections remain straightforward.


This fixed cost is paired with a tiered throughput system defined by[Perplexity](https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/admin/rate-limits-usage-tiers) :


- Tier 0: 1 query per second, which limits your initial testing to single-threaded sequential calls.
- Tier 1: 3 queries per second, providing enough overhead for your small team internal tools.
- Tier 2: 8 queries per second, allowing for moderate batch processing of data.
- Tier 3: 17 queries per second, supporting your real-time user-facing applications.
- Tiers 4-5: 33 queries per second, so your enterprise-scale workloads can process nearly 2,000 searches per minute.


### Why Perplexity search costs less than OpenAI or Tavily.


Perplexity’s search fee is often more economical because it bundles index access and LLM inference into a single round-trip.


By centralizing the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline, Perplexity eliminates the "double-tax" on tokens where the search results would otherwise be re-encoded as input context for a standalone model.
